passage: When people work in teams, they often assume that more communication is always better. Yet constant messaging, unplanned meetings, and endless status updates can fragment attention and slow down deep focus. High-performing teams tend to separate synchronous communication—used for alignment, decision-making, and complex problem-solving—from asynchronous communication, which allows members to share progress and work through tasks at their own pace. Clear norms around response times and documentation also prevent misunderstandings without forcing everyone to be online at the same moment. Ultimately, effective team collaboration depends not on how often people talk, but on whether communication matches the nature of the work.
